replies.reason: read_csv infers a numeric dtype for columns whose values all parse as numbers.

import pandas as pd

assert pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df['h'])

A comparison on a column gives a boolean Series, and df[mask] keeps the True rows.
replies.assert:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 5, 7]})
mask = df['a'] > 3

A column of numbers stays numeric when a cell is empty (it becomes NaN), but one non-numeric value makes the column text.
replies.assert:
import io
import pandas as pd
a = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO('n,p
a,1
b,
c,3
'))
assert pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(a['p'])
assert a['p'].isna().tolist() == [False, True, False]
b = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO('n,p
a,1
b,?
c,3
'))
assert not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(b['p'])

replies.reason: One value like ? stops the column being parsed as numbers, so every value stays a string.
replies.assert:
import io
import pandas as pd
b = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO('n,p\na,1\nb,?\nc,3\n'))
assert not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(b['p'])
assert b['p'].tolist() == ['1', '?', '3']

replies.reason: Adding strings joins them, and string order puts '10' before '9'.
replies.assert:
import io
import pandas as pd
b = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO('n,p\na,3\nb,?\nc,2\n'))
assert b['p'].astype(object).sum() == '3?2'
assert sorted(['9', '10']) == ['10', '9']
d = pd.DataFrame({'p': ['9', '10']}).sort_values('p')
assert d['p'].tolist() == ['10', '9']

replies.reason: to_numeric with errors='coerce' converts what it can and gives NaN for the rest.
replies.assert:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.to_numeric(pd.Series(['3', '?', '2']), errors='coerce')
assert pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s)
assert s.isna().tolist() == [False, True, False]
assert s.sum() == 5

replies.reason: Series sum and max skip NaN by default (skipna=True).
replies.assert:

import numpy as np
s = pd.Series([3.0, np.nan, 2.0])
assert s.sum() == 5.0
assert s.max() == 3.0

replies.reason: On text values, + joins the strings instead of adding numbers.
replies.assert:
import io
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO('p\n3\n?\n2\n'))
assert not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df['p'])
assert df['p'].iloc[0] + df['p'].iloc[2] == '32'
assert df['p'].astype(object).sum() == '3?2'
